summary: Mayor Lauren McLean proposed an emergency moratorium on “mega data centers” inside city limits. The city says no such application is pending. Council takes public comment Tuesday, November 10, at 6 p.m.
Emergency moratorium on data center applications and permits, a week after a 3.4 million sq ft concept reached City Hall. Idaho law caps emergency moratoriums at 182 days.
182-day emergency moratorium, passed 3-0 with no application pending, while staff draft zoning rules for three light-industrial zones, including one north of Hailey.
Council upheld, 3-2, its denial of Lex Developments’ $2.6 billion campus at the former Hoku plant, and waived the one-year wait to reapply. The developer has gone to court.

Council took up a code change banning data centers over 5,000 sq ft in the city’s industrial park zone, after its planning commission called the cap arbitrary. Local press reported approval on September 18; we could not open that report.
Commissioners unanimously adopted rules on water, power, noise and setbacks for future data centers. None exists or is proposed in the county.
Council voted 5-0 for a non-binding resolution opposing new or expanded data centers until the city finishes studying them. Zoning still allows them with a permit.
Council discussed a staff draft excluding data centers from city code. No vote taken.
180-day emergency moratorium for unincorporated areas, through January 26, 2027. A regional work group is drafting a model ordinance.

A 2025 moratorium, adopted to protect the Rathdrum Prairie Aquifer, expired in August 2025 and was replaced by an ordinance that keeps data centers off the aquifer. Commissioners said they wanted a total ban; we found no sign one passed.
